```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A has a lighter path to launch. Nothing is legally mandated before selling. SOC2 is described as commercially expected, not required, and a narrow Stripe-to-bank reconciliation scope can ship without it. B requires an IRS e-file Provider (EFIN) application with a suitability check, annual IRS software acceptance testing, and EU data-protection counsel. Those gates could plausibly consume much of a 90-day window.",
    "B's stated differentiator, filing correctly in the country of residence, is the part its own brief calls unsolved and very large in scope. The brief cites the most advanced competitor calling local products 'the hard part' and raises an open question about legal liability per country. If B retreats to US-only filing, it enters a commoditized field of six competitors priced from $67 to $219, with no wedge.",
    "A's revenue is monthly recurring at $29–100, so a single paying customer can come at any point in the 90 days. B is paid once per filing season, so its first-revenue timing depends on the season, and the brief offers no evidence of off-season demand.",
    "A has a cited low-cost distribution channel: the Stripe App Marketplace, which costs only dev and review time and reaches users who already have the reconciliation problem. It also has $0-cash Reddit and Indie Hackers channels where the pain is actively discussed. B's only cited channel is Meta lead-gen. The brief puts the blended CPL at $27.66 and says this niche likely runs higher.",
    "A's demand evidence is closely tied to the build. One source quantifies 3–4 hours per month spent on reconciliation, and another names specific pain items such as fees, refunds and failed payments. These map onto a mechanical, rules-based task that suits AI agents. B's demand quotes describe pain with US expat filing generally, not demand for the combined US-plus-local product it proposes."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's central 'case for' says Atamatax, a solo-built tool, can charge $199–$799 and 'attract customers.' The only source given is Atamatax's own pricing page. That shows a listed price, not paying customers or traction, so the claimed proof that a one-person build works rests on unsourced inference. B also offers no evidence that anyone wants or would pay for the combined US-plus-local-country filing that is its differentiator.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A has serious unresolved weaknesses. It faces six or more direct competitors, including free tiers that the brief says likely cover solo-founder volumes, and it has no clear wedge. The $400–600/mo Growthy estimate is cited without a link, and its data-privacy obligations are marked [unsourced]. A wins mainly because B's regulatory gates, seasonal payment timing and unbuildable differentiator are larger obstacles to a first paying customer within 90 days, not because A's case is strong on its own."
}
```
